memos.scout:
Case for buying now is weak, and I don't think it clears the bar.

The strongest point is the last 15 minutes: 193 buyers against 176 sellers, net flow +11.7 SOL, and a +47% return. That's a real bounce from a 75.7% drawdown, and the class is tagged ORGANIC with no airdrop dump seen. Buyer count is high (1,086) and top-3 holder concentration is low (5.9%).

But the rest undercuts it. The 30-minute return is -56%, and the 15-minute bounce is a single window that could be a dead-cat move. Bundle share is 39.8% and the completer share is 32%, which suggests much of the early activity was coordinated rather than independent demand. Sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.94, and the 15-minute window shows $67 SOL sold against $79 SOL bought, so sellers are nearly keeping pace. The pool is thin at 56 SOL, so a $20 ticket plus 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs and 30 seconds of latency means the entry price could be materially worse than the decision-time price.

Against a base rate of roughly -20% for random post-graduation buys, a single bounce window doesn't establish that demand will persist for the next 30-60 minutes. Verdict: no clear case. Skip.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss path: a dead-cat bounce that bleeds out to fees. The coin is down 75.7% from its 30-minute high and 56% over the window, and the last 15 minutes show a +47% "return" that is mostly churn: 193 buyers against 176 sellers, with 67.42 SOL sold versus 79.12 SOL bought. Net flow of only 11.7 SOL on a 56.5 SOL pool means the rally is thin and sellers are waiting to exit into it.

Insider distribution is also plausible. The bundle share is 39.8% and the completer share is 32.3%, so a bundled group of wallets likely holds a large stake. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.938 in the first two minutes after graduation shows heavy early selling.

With a 30-second execution delay and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost on a $21k cap, a bounce of a few percent is unlikely to clear fees before the next leg down.
